subject.title: [Bug]: Slack reaction_added/reaction_removed events never delivered via Socket Mode (multi-account, v2026.3.24)

question: Should maintainers keep this as the canonical reaction-specific Slack Socket Mode diagnosis until live envelope proof exists, or fold it into broader Slack Socket Mode liveness work now?
rationale: Current source proves handler support but not the reported live zero-envelope failure, and choosing the repair path requires knowing whether reactions are never delivered, filtered by account metadata, authorized away, or lost during a broader socket stall.

options.title: Keep Reaction-Specific Canonical
options.body: Keep this issue open and request redacted current-main reaction envelopes plus gateway trace logs before any code repair is queued.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Liveness
options.body: Route follow-up through the broader Slack Socket Mode liveness issue only if live diagnostics show all event families stall together rather than reactions failing alone.

options.title: Close After Live Pass
options.body: Close as fixed only if a maintainer verifies current main or a shipped release receives `reaction_added` and `reaction_removed` envelopes in a comparable multi-account Socket Mode setup.

recommendation.title: Keep Reaction-Specific Canonical
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and request redacted current-main reaction envelopes plus gateway trace logs before any code repair is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: The Slack monitor history and mismatch-filter ownership make this the strongest routing target for deciding the proof bar and canonical issue shape.
